resources.string: Looking for the HUD on this Wi-Fi…
Connected to %1$s — not paired: without a pairing code nothing proves this is your HUD
A different HUD is answering at %1$s (%2$s…, not your paired HUD %3$s…). Nothing was sent to it.

The HUD at %1$s (%2$s…, certificate %3$s) has no pairing code, so the app cannot verify that it is yours. Connect only if it is: the HUD\'s settings show its certificate under Phone. Better, set a pairing code there and enter it in Setup.
The HUD at %1$s could not prove that it knows your pairing code. Nothing was sent to it. Check the code in Setup.
The HUD at %1$s broke the handshake (%2$s). Nothing was sent to it.

HUD certificate changed — re-pair. The HUD at %1$s presented certificate %2$s instead of the paired %3$s. Nothing was sent to it, and the app stops trying. If you reset or replaced the HUD, forget it and pair again; otherwise another device may be posing as your HUD.
The HUD at %1$s presented certificate %2$s, not the one it announces on the network (%3$s): something between the phone and the HUD is answering. Nothing was sent to it.
Replaced or reset your HUD? Forget the paired one: the next HUD that proves your pairing code becomes the paired HUD.
Messages are read aloud on the phone
Messages are not read aloud (HUD or app setting)
Android did not allow starting the service. Try again with the app open.
Google Maps turn-by-turn, message senders and the music you play
If Android says this setting is restricted: open App settings, tap ⋮ and choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.
Show incoming calls with the number; accept or decline from the HUD
Show the caller\'s name instead of the number
GPS for the HUD, speed limits and speed cameras
Connection status, logged trips and maintenance reminders
Keeps the connection alive while the screen is off
Not connected over the live link; buttons are sent through the HUD\'s web API.
No trips yet. Trips are logged by the HUD and appear here after each drive.
No maintenance items configured on the HUD.
Uses mDNS (_carheadsup._tcp) on the car\'s Wi-Fi
Enter an address like 192.168.4.1 or hud.local:8443 (the HUD\'s TLS port)

Pair by scanning the code on the HUD: park, then open its \"Pair a phone\" page (in the HUD\'s settings: Phone → Show pairing code on the HUD, or page to the dashboard\'s last page). Or enter the pairing code by hand below.
Point the camera at the QR code on the HUD\'s display.
That is not a carheadsup pairing code. Scan the code on the HUD\'s \"Pair a phone\" page.
That pairing code did not read correctly. Hold the phone a little closer and steadier.
This HUD shows a newer kind of pairing code. Update the carheadsup app, or enter the pairing code by hand below.
The camera is needed only to scan the code. Allow it, or enter the pairing code by hand below.
The camera could not be started (%1$s). Enter the pairing code by hand below.
Paired with %1$s (certificate %2$s). It is not reachable yet at %3$s: join the car\'s Wi-Fi and the app connects.
Set by scanning the HUD\'s code, or as shown in the HUD\'s settings (Phone → Pairing code). It is never sent: phone and HUD prove to each other that they know it.
Confirmed HUD %1$s… (no pairing code: not verified)
Confirmed HUD %1$s… · certificate %2$s (no pairing code: not verified)
Not paired yet: the first HUD that proves this code is remembered.
No pairing code: nothing proves which HUD answers, so you confirm it on the Status tab. Set a code on the HUD instead.
For trips, maintenance and the settings page; empty if the HUD has none
The HUD shows only who wrote; the phone reads the message while connected
Used for night mode by sun position and for context
Looks up map data around you (uses mobile data)
Mapped cameras ahead. Off by default: such warnings are illegal while driving in some countries (e.g. Germany, Switzerland). Check local law before turning them on.
Jams, accidents, closures and road works up to about 10 km ahead, with the expected delay. Needs your own free TomTom API key; uses mobile data.
From developer.tomtom.com. The free plan allows 2,500 requests a day; the app makes at most 2,000.
A TomTom API key is a string of letters and digits (32 of them).

Privacy: while traffic is on and you drive, the phone sends TomTom the area around and ahead of the car (about 10 × 6 km) with your API key, every 2 minutes or so. TomTom can tell from this where you drive.
Enter and save your TomTom API key to get traffic.
Starts when the app connects to the HUD.
Waiting for GPS and the direction of travel…
Paused while the car stands still; resumes when you drive on.
TomTom did not answer (%1$s); trying again shortly.
TomTom refused the API key (%1$s). Check the key: traffic stays off until you save another one or switch traffic off and on.
Today\'s request budget is used up; traffic resumes after midnight UTC.
Layouts, units, alerts and projection are configured on the HUD itself.
Connect to your HUD first: the settings page only opens on a HUD that has proven itself (it receives the API token).
Not opened: the HUD presented certificate %1$s, not the paired %2$s, so nothing was sent to it. If you reset or replaced the HUD, forget it in the app and pair again.
Not opened: the HUD\'s certificate could not be checked, so nothing was sent to it.
Shown while the app keeps the connection to the HUD
A different HUD is answering — nothing was sent. Open the app.
A HUD without pairing code is waiting for your confirmation
The HUD could not prove the pairing code — nothing was sent
HUD certificate changed — re-pair. Nothing was sent. Open the app.
The HUD\'s certificate is not the announced one — nothing was sent
A summary when the HUD logs a trip
Oil changes and other service that is due
